title: Rescue a deleted branch, a reset commit and a stash

ticket.subject: I think I destroyed two days of work, please help
body: I was cleaning up the repository last night and I went too far:
1. I deleted `feature/quarterly-report` with `git branch -D`. It had two commits that were never pushed.
2. Then I ran `git reset --hard HEAD~1` on main to undo something, and the runbook commit
(`docs: add the on-call runbook`) disappeared with it.
3. Before all that I had stashed a change to `config.yml` (retries from 3 to 5).
- bring back `feature/quarterly-report` exactly as it was (its two commits, same content);
- put the runbook commit back on main;
- apply my stashed change and commit it on main as `chore: raise retries to 5`, and leave the stash empty;
- nothing else: main is the four commits (the initial import, the nightly job, the runbook, the retries), linear.
Git keeps a journal of where HEAD has been. I hope it is in there.

acceptance.text: feature/quarterly-report is back with its two commits.
The runbook commit is back on main.
The stashed change is committed on main as "chore: raise retries to 5", and the stash is empty.
main is exactly the four commits, linear; the report branch is not merged into it.
Nothing is in progress and the tree is clean.

hints: `git reflog` lists every position HEAD had, newest first: commits, checkouts, the reset. The commits of a deleted branch are still there as long as the reflog points at them.
`git branch <name> <commit>` creates a branch at any commit, including one only the reflog still knows (`HEAD@{5}` or its hash).

`git reset --hard <commit>` moves main back to a commit the reflog shows, which undoes a reset. `HEAD@{n}` names the n-th entry, but read the list first: the stash left an entry of its own. Check with `git log --oneline`.
`git stash list` shows the stash; `git stash pop` applies the newest entry and drops it, `git stash apply` keeps it. Then commit the change.
